slides.say: A school has N students, and g of them are girls. Twenty-five percent of the girls play chess. What percent of all the students are girls who play chess?
There are letters in the question and in the choices. That's a hint that we can plug in numbers. We'll solve it in two different ways, by plugging in numbers, and then the math way.
Let's start by plugging in numbers. Like in psychometric thinking, check the restrictions first. Then choose easy allowed numbers. If choices give the same result, try another allowed example.

Let's say there are two hundred students, so N is two hundred. And eighty of them are girls, so g is eighty. Why eighty? Because a quarter of eighty is a whole number, and eighty is less than two hundred.
Twenty-five percent of the girls play chess. A quarter of eighty is twenty girls.
Now, what percent of all the students is that? Twenty out of two hundred is ten out of a hundred, ten percent. So our target is ten percent.

Now we put N is two hundred and g is eighty into every choice. Choice number one says g over four N percent. Four times two hundred is eight hundred, so it's eighty over eight hundred percent. That's a tenth of a percent, not ten percent. Out.

Choice number two says a hundred g over N percent. A hundred times eighty is eight thousand, and eight thousand over two hundred is forty. That's forty percent of the students, all the girls, not just the girls who play chess. Out.
at: not just the girls who play chess

slides.say: Choice number three says twenty-five g over N percent. Twenty-five times eighty is two thousand, and two thousand over two hundred is ten. So this choice gives ten percent, our target.
at: Twenty-five times eighty is two thousand
two thousand over two hundred is ten

slides.say: In the exam you'd circle it and move on. Here, let's check the last one too. Choice number four says twenty-five N over g percent. Twenty-five times two hundred is five thousand. Five thousand over eighty is more than sixty, because eighty times sixty is only four thousand eight hundred. So it's more than sixty percent, not ten percent. Out.
at: So it's more than sixty percent

slides.say: Only choice number three gives ten percent. If two choices had given ten percent, we'd pick new numbers and test only those two. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the math way, with the letters. We start again from the givens. Twenty-five percent of the girls is a quarter of g, so g over four girls play chess.
To get a percent, we take the part over the whole, times a hundred. The part is g over four, and the whole is all the students, N.
at: we take the part over the whole

slides.say: g over four, divided by N, is g over four N.
Times a hundred, it's a hundred g over four N. A hundred over four is twenty-five, so it's twenty-five g over N.
at: A hundred over four is twenty-five

slides.say: g over four N is the fraction of the students. To write it as a percent, we multiply that number by a hundred first. Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
